source_text: אַחֲרָי/ו֙ הֶחֱזִ֣יקוּ אֲחֵי/הֶ֔ם בַּוַּ֖י בֶּן חֵנָדָ֑ד שַׂ֕ר חֲצִ֖י פֶּ֥לֶךְ קְעִילָֽה־׃ס
english_snapshot: After him their brothers repaired: Bavvai son of Henadad[a], ruler of half the district of Keilah.

signals.text: Some textual traditions read the name as 'Binnui' instead of 'Bavvai.'

source_text: אחר/י הֶחֱזִ֜יק חֲנַנְיָ֣ה בֶן שֶׁלֶמְיָ֗ה וְ/חָנ֧וּן בֶּן צָלָ֛ף הַ/שִּׁשִּׁ֖י מִדָּ֣ה שֵׁנִ֑י אַחֲרָ֣י/ו הֶחֱזִ֗יק מְשֻׁלָּם֙ בֶּן בֶּ֣רֶכְיָ֔ה נֶ֖גֶד נִשְׁכָּתֽ/וֹ־־ס־׃ס
english_snapshot: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph repaired another section[b][a]. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his chamber.

signals.text: The first phrase is traditionally understood in context as 'After him,' matching the repeated sequence formula in this chapter.

source_text: וְ/אֵ֗לֶּה הָֽ/עוֹלִים֙ מִ/תֵּ֥ל מֶ֨לַח֙ תֵּ֣ל חַרְשָׁ֔א כְּר֥וּב אַדּ֖וֹן וְ/אִמֵּ֑ר וְ/לֹ֣א יָכְל֗וּ לְ/הַגִּ֤יד בֵּית אֲבוֹתָ/ם֙ וְ/זַרְעָ֔/ם אִ֥ם מִ/יִּשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵֽם־׃
english_snapshot: And these were the ones who came up from Tel-melah[a], Tel-harsha, Kerub, Addon, and Immer, but they were not able to declare their fathers’ houses or their offspring[c][b], whether they were from Israel.

signals.text: Ezra 2:59 reads 'Addan' where Nehemiah here has 'Addon.'

source_text: וּ/מִ/קְצָת֙ רָאשֵׁ֣י הָֽ/אָב֔וֹת נָתְנ֖וּ לַ/מְּלָאכָ֑ה הַ/תִּרְשָׁ֜תָא נָתַ֣ן לָ/אוֹצָ֗ר זָהָ֞ב דַּרְכְּמֹנִ֥ים אֶ֨לֶף֙ מִזְרָק֣וֹת חֲמִשִּׁ֔ים כָּתְנוֹת֙ כֹּֽהֲנִ֔ים שְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים וַ/חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃
english_snapshot: And some of the heads of the fathers’ houses gave to the work[a]. The governor gave to the treasury one thousand gold darics, fifty basins[c][b], and five hundred thirty-five priests’ tunics.

signals.text: Hebrew reads 'five hundred thirty-five priests’ tunics.' The parallel in Ezra 2:69 reads 'one hundred priests’ tunics,' and some translations harmonize or reflect a different textual tradition.

source_text: וְ/אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן סַלֻּ֡א בֶּן מְשֻׁלָּ֡ם בֶּן יוֹעֵ֡ד בֶּן פְּדָיָה֩ בֶן ק֨וֹלָיָ֧ה בֶן מַעֲשֵׂיָ֛ה בֶּן אִֽיתִיאֵ֖ל בֶּן יְשַֽׁעְיָֽה־־־־־־־׃
english_snapshot: And these were the sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam[a], son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel[b], son of Jeshaiah.

signals.text: The name 'Joed' follows the Masoretic Text here. A parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 9:7 reads 'Hodaviah.'

source_text: וְ/יוֹיָדָע֙ הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת יוֹנָתָ֔ן וְ/יוֹנָתָ֖ן הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת יַדּֽוּעַ־־׃
english_snapshot: And Joiada fathered Jonathan[a], and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.

signals.text: Some manuscripts and translations read 'Johanan' instead of 'Jonathan.' The Hebrew text used here reads 'Jonathan.'

source_text: וּ/בְ/כָל זֶ֕ה לֹ֥א הָיִ֖יתִי בִּֽ/ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם כִּ֡י בִּ/שְׁנַת֩ שְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וּ/שְׁתַּ֜יִם לְ/אַרְתַּחְשַׁ֤סְתְּא מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶל֙ בָּ֣אתִי אֶל הַ/מֶּ֔לֶךְ וּ/לְ/קֵ֥ץ יָמִ֖ים נִשְׁאַ֥לְתִּי מִן הַ/מֶּֽלֶךְ־־־־׃
english_snapshot: But during all this I was not in Jerusalem[a], for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I went to the king[b], and after some time I asked leave from the king.

signals.text: Hebrew: 'king of Babylon.' The text is translated as written rather than harmonized to the broader Persian imperial setting.
